subject: Invoice discrepancy — weekly rollup mismatch & VAT treatment (WavePay)
messages:
From: Marta Kaczmarek <marta@wavepay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: WavePay Finance <finance@wavepay.com>
Date: 2026-11-07 09:12 +01:00
Subject: Discrepancy on Nov weekly invoice (tokens spike)

Hi Hannah —

We received the invoice for the period Nov 1–7 and see a ~13% increase in billed tokens compared with our internal counters. The spike is concentrated around the nightly batch that runs at ~01:00 UTC (our processing job replays embeddings). I attached the invoice (invoice-20261101.pdf) and a quick export from our side (wavepay-usage-2026-11-01_to_11-07.csv).

Two quick asks: can Redwood provide a per-route token breakdown for that week (especially for the embed.indexing route) and confirm whether any reprocessing retries on your side could have caused double-counting? Also, we are an EU entity — please confirm VAT treatment; this item looks like it may need reverse-charge treatment in our next statement.

We'd like to avoid holds on payment if possible but need an explanation before we finalize.

Thanks,
Marta
Finance Lead — WavePay
--
WavePay | finance@wavepay.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kaczmarek <marta@wavepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07 10:05 +01:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Nov weekly invoice (tokens spike)

Hi Marta — thanks for flagging this and for sending your export + the invoice. I'm looping in Ben (your account lead) and Laura from billing so we can get you a per-route breakdown and an initial assessment.

Ben / Laura — can one of you confirm whether there were any backend retries or ingest replays during that window (Nov 3 overnight) and produce a vetted usage export? If it helps, WavePay has called out the embed.indexing route specifically.

We'll aim to get a preliminary response by EOD Tuesday (Nov 9). If an error on our side is confirmed we'll propose a provisional credit right away.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kaczmarek <marta@wavepay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08 08:45 +01:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Nov weekly invoice (tokens spike)

Marta — thanks for the detailed note. I chatted briefly with Ops this morning. Two quick items while we investigate:

- Can you confirm whether WavePay ran any parallel replay jobs on Nov 3 that would have re-sent the same session IDs to our API? That would be the fastest explanation.
- We're happy to place a provisional credit against your account for the disputed amount while we validate. Would you prefer a credit to the next invoice or a one-time refund?

If you can send the raw request IDs (or the small excerpt of your replay log) that will speed things up. Laura — if our usage export lines up with their CSV we can set a provisional credit today; otherwise reserve until we finish reconciliation.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kaczmarek <marta@wavepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09 14:30 +01:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Nov weekly invoice (tokens spike)

Hi Marta — I've pulled the usage ledger and performed an initial reconciliation (see attached usage-export-wavepay-20261101-11-07.csv). Summary of findings:

- Scope: embed.indexing and ingest.bulk routes.
- Root cause (preliminary): between 01:00–02:15 UTC on 2026-11-03 our ingestion queue experienced a transient ACK timeout on a single shard which caused the client-side retry handler to resubmit ~18% of batches. Because the retry payloads did not include the original session metadata, our deduplication window (which requires session_id) could not suppress the replays, resulting in double-counting of those tokens.
- Impact: net increase of 1,040,762 tokens for the weekly period across your account, concentrated on Nov 3.
- Proposed correction: we recommend a one-time credit for 1,040,762 tokens at your contracted rate (€0.00123/token) = €1,280.17 (net).

VAT notes: because WavePay is an EU-registered business and has provided a valid VAT number on file, Redwood will treat this adjustment under the reverse-charge mechanism. We will send an adjusted invoice reflecting the credit and mark it for reverse charge; please confirm that your VAT number on file (PL-123456789) is still valid.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether you prefer the credit applied to the next invoice or a direct refund (we can do either).
2) If refund, provide the beneficiary and bank details; for credit we'll post the adjustment and issue an updated invoice (adjusted PDF attached placeholder).
3) We will run a deeper post-mortem and share the full timeline by Nov 16.

Attachments: usage-export-wavepay-20261101-11-07.csv; (proposed_adjustment_20261103.pdf placeholder)

If you'd like, we can also run a token-level sample to show the duplicated request_ids.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Billing Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference — billing@redwood.com
From: Marta Kaczmarek <marta@wavepay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-11 15:03 +01:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Nov weekly invoice (tokens spike)

Hi Laura / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear breakdown. We checked our side and we did indeed have a replay window on Nov 3 that re-submitted failed batches; attached is our retry log excerpt (wavepay-retry-log-20261103.txt).

We'd prefer to take the credit applied to the next invoice rather than a refund. VAT number PL-123456789 is current. Please post the adjustment and send the updated invoice (reverse-charge).

Appreciate the provisional offer — please go ahead and post the credit; we'll settle the remainder of the invoice on schedule.

Best,
Marta
